parties:
SMA Matin Sarker ------ Petitioner
vs
Bangladesh Jute Mills Association and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 6. Mr Md Asaduzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.1, made a straight forward argument to refute the contention raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. Mr Asaduzzaman submits that it is now well settled that the past salary and emoluments of an employee cannot be termed as debts within the intents and meaning of subsection (v) of section 24;1 of the Act. He further submits that a debt is a sum of money which is now payable or will be payable in future by a person. He, in elaborating his submission, submits that in the instant case the petitioner filed a petition for winding up of the Association in which he was an employee holding the post of Senior Executive at the relevant time and the instant petition is absolutely misconceived, firstly, because the claim is highly disputed and secondly, the salary does not come within the ambit of a "debt" as there is a difference between a debt and salary. He further elaborates his submission by submitting that the salary or remuneration is paid to a person or an employee in lieu of service rendered by him or her, whereas debt is not remuneration but something which is borrowed by a person on settled terms and conditions and settled rate of interest and can be resettled between the parties. Therefore, the instant application does not come within the ambit of sub-section (v) of section 241 of the Act. Mr Asaduzzaman, to substantiate the aforesaid contention, relied on the decision reported in AIR 1996 MP 85 and also relies on the case reported in 68 Company Cases, 264 Karnataka. Mr Asaduzzaman finally submits that since the instant application has been filed for winding up of the Association on the ground of its inability to pay the debt of the petitioner and since the alleged claim of the petitioner does not amount to a debt, the petitioner cannot maintain the same and he may however, go to the Civil Court to establish his claim and then, if a decree is passed in favour of him for a certain amount, he may then become creditor within the meaning of section 242 of the Act and not otherwise.
